column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)
bio|11-04|1957|Τόνι Άμποτ|Tony Abbott|Tony Abbott is an Australian politician. He was born in London and was prime minister of Australia from 2013 to 2015, as leader of the Liberal Party.

bio|11-04|1969|Μάθιου Μακόναχι|Matthew McConaughey|Matthew McConaughey is an American actor. He won an Oscar for "Dallas Buyers Club" and appeared in "Interstellar" and in the series "True Detective".
bio|11-04|1972|Λουίς Φίγκο|Luís Figo|Luís Figo is a former Portuguese footballer, a midfielder. He played for Barcelona, Real Madrid and Inter, and in 2000 he won the Ballon d'Or.

bio|11-04|1995|Γιτζάκ Ράμπιν|Yitzhak Rabin|Yitzhak Rabin was an Israeli military officer and politician. As prime minister he signed the Oslo Accords with the Palestinians, and in 1994 he shared the Nobel Peace Prize. He was assassinated in 1995 by an Israeli nationalist.

bio|11-04|1995|Ζιλ Ντελέζ|Gilles Deleuze|Gilles Deleuze was a French philosopher. He wrote "Difference and Repetition" and, together with Félix Guattari, "Anti-Oedipus" and "A Thousand Plateaus". He died in 1995.
bio|11-05|1615|Ιμπραήμ Α΄|Ibrahim I|Ibrahim I was Ottoman sultan from 1640 to 1648. During his reign the siege of Crete began. He was deposed and executed in 1648.

bio|11-05|1855|Γιουτζίν Ντεμπς|Eugene Debs|Eugene Debs was an American trade unionist and politician. He founded the railway workers' union and was the Socialist Party's candidate for the presidency five times. He died in 1926.

bio|11-05|1879|Τζέιμς Κλερκ Μάξγουελ|James Clerk Maxwell|James Clerk Maxwell was a Scottish physicist. He formulated Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism and showed that light is an electromagnetic wave. He died in 1879, at the age of 48.
bio|11-05|1913|Βίβιαν Λι|Vivien Leigh|Vivien Leigh was an English actress. She won two Oscars, for "Gone with the Wind" and "A Streetcar Named Desire". She died in 1967.

bio|11-05|1944|Αλεξίς Καρέλ|Alexis Carrel|Alexis Carrel was a French surgeon and biologist. He developed methods of suturing blood vessels and in 1912 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. He died in 1944.
bio|11-05|1959|Μπράιαν Άνταμς|Bryan Adams|Bryan Adams is a Canadian singer-songwriter and rock singer. He became known with hits such as "Summer of '69" and "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You".

bio|11-05|1960|Τίλντα Σουίντον|Tilda Swinton|Tilda Swinton is an English actress. She won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "Michael Clayton" and appeared in "Doctor Strange" and "Snowpiercer".
bio|11-05|1997|Αϊζάια Μπερλίν|Isaiah Berlin|Isaiah Berlin was a British philosopher, born in Riga. He wrote "Two Concepts of Liberty" and supported the pluralism of values. He died in 1997.

bio|11-05|2006|Μπουλέντ Ετζεβίτ|Bülent Ecevit|Bülent Ecevit was a Turkish politician and poet. He was prime minister of Turkey on several occasions and ordered the invasion of Cyprus in 1974. He died in 2006.

bio|11-06|331|Ιουλιανός|Julian|Julian was Roman emperor from 361 to 363. He was the nephew of Constantine and tried to restore pagan worship, which is why he was called "the Apostate". He was killed on a campaign against the Persians. The exact year of his birth is 331 or 332.

bio|11-06|1494|Σουλεϊμάν Α΄ ο Μεγαλοπρεπής|Suleiman I the Magnificent|Suleiman I was Ottoman sultan from 1520 to 1566. He conquered Belgrade and Rhodes and reached the gates of Vienna. During his reign the empire reached its height.
bio|11-06|1656|Ιωάννης Δ΄|John IV of Portugal|John IV was king of Portugal from 1640, the first of the Braganza dynasty, after the restoration of independence from Spain. He died in 1656.
bio|11-06|1814|Αντόλφ Σαξ|Adolphe Sax|Adolphe Sax was a Belgian maker of musical instruments. He invented the saxophone in the 1840s. He died in 1894.
bio|11-06|1836|Κάρολος Ι΄|Charles X|Charles X was king of France from 1824 to 1830. He was overthrown by the July Revolution, went into exile and died in 1836 in Gorizia.

bio|11-06|1893|Πιότρ Τσαϊκόφσκι|Pyotr Tchaikovsky|Pyotr Tchaikovsky was a Russian composer. He wrote the ballets "Swan Lake" and "The Nutcracker" and the "Pathétique" Symphony. He died in 1893 in Saint Petersburg.
bio|11-06|1946|Σάλι Φιλντ|Sally Field|Sally Field is an American actress. She won two Oscars, for "Norma Rae" and "Places in the Heart".

bio|11-06|1960|Έριχ Ραίντερ|Erich Raeder|Erich Raeder was a German admiral. He was commander of the German navy during the Second World War until 1943 and was sentenced at the Nuremberg trial. He died in 1960.
bio|11-06|1988|Έμμα Στόουν|Emma Stone|Emma Stone is an American actress. She won an Oscar for "La La Land" and for "Poor Things", and she also appeared in "The Favourite".

bio|11-03|644|Ουμάρ ιμπν αλ-Χαττάμπ|Umar ibn al-Khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab was the second caliph of Islam, from 634. During his reign the Arabs conquered Syria, Egypt and Persia. He was assassinated in 644.

bio|11-07|1728|Τζέιμς Κουκ|James Cook|James Cook was a British explorer and cartographer. He led three expeditions in the Pacific and mapped New Zealand and eastern Australia. He was killed in 1779 in Hawaii.

bio|11-07|1867|Μαρία Κιουρί|Marie Curie|Marie Curie was born in 1867 in Warsaw. She was a physicist and chemist and was awarded two Nobel Prizes, in Physics in 1903 and in Chemistry in 1911. She died in 1934.
bio|11-07|1879|Λέων Τρότσκι|Leon Trotsky|Leon Trotsky was a Russian revolutionary. He was head of the Red Army and an opponent of Stalin. He was exiled and assassinated in 1940 in Mexico.

bio|11-07|1888|Τσαντρασεκάρα Ράμαν|C. V. Raman|C. V. Raman was an Indian physicist. He discovered the Raman effect, concerning the scattering of light, and in 1930 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1970.

bio|11-07|1913|Αλμπέρ Καμύ|Albert Camus|Albert Camus was born in 1913 in Algeria. He was a French writer and philosopher. He wrote "The Stranger", "The Myth of Sisyphus" and "The Plague", and in 1957 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1960.

bio|11-07|1913|Άλφρεντ Ράσελ Γουάλας|Alfred Russel Wallace|Alfred Russel Wallace was a Welsh biologist and naturalist. Independently of Darwin, he formulated the theory of evolution through natural selection and studied the global geographical distribution of animals. He died in 1913.

bio|11-07|1962|Έλινορ Ρούζβελτ|Eleanor Roosevelt|Eleanor Roosevelt was the wife of President Franklin Roosevelt and an activist. She contributed to the drafting of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. She died in 1962.
bio|11-07|2016|Λέοναρντ Κόεν|Leonard Cohen|Leonard Cohen was a Canadian poet and singer-songwriter. He wrote songs such as "Suzanne" and "Hallelujah". He died in 2016, at the age of 82.

bio|11-08|1656|Έντμουντ Χάλλεϋ|Edmond Halley|Edmond Halley was an English astronomer and mathematician. He calculated the orbit of the comet that bears his name and encouraged Newton to publish the "Principia". He died in 1742.
bio|11-08|1674|Τζον Μίλτον|John Milton|John Milton was an English poet. He wrote the epic "Paradise Lost" and "Areopagitica", in favour of freedom of the press. He lost his sight and died in 1674.
bio|11-08|1847|Μπραμ Στόκερ|Bram Stoker|Bram Stoker was an Irish writer. He wrote the novel "Dracula" in 1897, which became the model for many vampire stories. He died in 1912.
bio|11-08|1900|Μάργκαρετ Μίτσελ|Margaret Mitchell|Margaret Mitchell was an American writer. Her only novel, "Gone with the Wind", won the Pulitzer Prize and became a famous film. She died in 1949.
bio|11-08|1935|Αλέν Ντελόν|Alain Delon|Alain Delon was a French actor. He became known for the films "Rocco and His Brothers", "The Black Knight" and "Le Samouraï". He died in 2024.
bio|11-08|1953|Ιβάν Μπούνιν|Ivan Bunin|Ivan Bunin died in 1953 in Paris. He was a Russian writer who lived in exile. In 1933 he became the first Russian to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|11-08|1954|Καζούο Ισιγκούρο|Kazuo Ishiguro|Kazuo Ishiguro was born in Japan and grew up in England. He wrote the novels "The Remains of the Day" and "Never Let Me Go". In 2017 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|11-08|1986|Βιατσεσλάβ Μόλοτοφ|Vyacheslav Molotov|Vyacheslav Molotov was a Soviet politician. He was foreign minister under Stalin and signed the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact in 1939. He died in 1986.

bio|11-08|2009|Βιτάλι Γκίνζμπουργκ|Vitaly Ginzburg|Vitaly Ginzburg was a Russian physicist. He contributed to the theory of superconductivity and in 2003 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 2009.
bio|11-09|1818|Ιβάν Τουργκένιεφ|Ivan Turgenev|Ivan Turgenev was a Russian writer. He wrote "Fathers and Sons" and "A Sportsman's Sketches". He died in 1883.
bio|11-09|1841|Εδουάρδος Ζ΄|Edward VII|Edward VII was king of the United Kingdom from 1901 to 1910. He was the son of Queen Victoria and his era was named the "Edwardian" era. He died in 1910.

bio|11-09|1914|Χέντι Λαμάρ|Hedy Lamarr|Hedy Lamarr was an Austrian actress and inventor. She appeared in Hollywood films and developed, together with George Antheil, a frequency-hopping system, a forerunner of Wi-Fi. She died in 2000.
bio|11-09|1918|Γκυγιώμ Απολλιναίρ|Guillaume Apollinaire|Guillaume Apollinaire died in 1918 in Paris, of influenza. He was a French poet and introduced the term "surrealism".

bio|11-09|1929|Ίμρε Κέρτες|Imre Kertész|Imre Kertész was a Hungarian writer and an Auschwitz survivor. He wrote the novel "Fatelessness" and in 2002 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2016.

bio|11-09|1934|Καρλ Σαγκάν|Carl Sagan|Carl Sagan was an American astronomer and science writer. He wrote "Cosmos" and presented the television series of the same name, and he contributed to the programme for exploring the Solar System. He died in 1996.

bio|11-09|1940|Νέβιλ Τσάμπερλεν|Neville Chamberlain|Neville Chamberlain was a British politician. As prime minister he signed the Munich Agreement in 1938, and his policy of appeasing Hitler was regarded as a failure. He resigned in 1940 and died the same year.
bio|11-09|1953|Ιμπν Σαούντ|Ibn Saud|Abdulaziz ibn Saud was the founder and first king of Saudi Arabia, in 1932. He united the regions of the Arabian Peninsula. He died in 1953.

bio|11-09|1970|Σαρλ ντε Γκωλ|Charles de Gaulle|Charles de Gaulle was a French general and politician. He led Free France in the Second World War and was president of France from 1959 to 1969. He died in 1970.

bio|11-10|1483|Μαρτίνος Λούθηρος|Martin Luther|Martin Luther was a German monk and theologian. In 1517 he published the "Ninety-five Theses" and the Protestant Reformation began. He translated the Bible into German. He died in 1546.

bio|11-10|1759|Φρίντριχ Σίλερ|Friedrich Schiller|Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and playwright. He wrote "The Robbers" and "William Tell", and the poem "Ode to Joy", which Beethoven set to music. He died in 1805.
bio|11-10|1891|Αρθούρος Ρεμπώ|Arthur Rimbaud|Arthur Rimbaud died in 1891 in Marseille. He was a French poet of Symbolism and stopped writing at the age of twenty.

bio|11-10|1919|Μιχαήλ Καλάσνικοφ|Mikhail Kalashnikov|Mikhail Kalashnikov was a Russian soldier and weapons designer. He created the AK-47 rifle, one of the most widespread weapons in the world. He died in 2013.

bio|11-10|1925|Ρίτσαρντ Μπάρτον|Richard Burton|Richard Burton was a Welsh actor. He appeared in the films "Cleopatra" and "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?". He was married to Elizabeth Taylor. He died in 1984.

bio|11-10|1928|Ένιο Μορικόνε|Ennio Morricone|Ennio Morricone was an Italian composer. He wrote the music for more than 400 films, among them "The Good, the Bad and the Ugly" and "Once Upon a Time in America". He died in 2020.

bio|11-10|1938|Μουσταφά Κεμάλ Ατατούρκ|Mustafa Kemal Atatürk|Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was a Turkish military officer and politician. He founded the Turkish Republic in 1923 and was its first president. He died in 1938 in Istanbul.

bio|11-10|1982|Λεονίντ Μπρέζνιεφ|Leonid Brezhnev|Leonid Brezhnev was a Soviet politician. He was general secretary of the Communist Party from 1964 until his death in 1982, and his period is called "stagnation".
bio|11-10|2015|Χέλμουτ Σμιτ|Helmut Schmidt|Helmut Schmidt was a German Social Democrat politician. He was chancellor of West Germany from 1974 to 1982. He died in 2015.
bio|11-11|1821|Φιόντορ Ντοστογιέφσκι|Fyodor Dostoevsky|Fyodor Dostoevsky was a Russian writer. He wrote the novels "Crime and Punishment", "The Idiot" and "The Brothers Karamazov". He died in 1881.

bio|11-11|1855|Σαίρεν Κίρκεγκωρ|Søren Kierkegaard|Søren Kierkegaard was a Danish philosopher and theologian. He is regarded as a forerunner of existentialism and wrote "Fear and Trembling" and "The Sickness unto Death". He died in 1855.
bio|11-11|1922|Κουρτ Βόνεγκατ|Kurt Vonnegut|Kurt Vonnegut was an American writer. He wrote the novel "Slaughterhouse-Five", based on his experience of the bombing of Dresden. He died in 2007.
bio|11-11|1962|Ντέμι Μουρ|Demi Moore|Demi Moore is an American actress. She became known for the films "Ghost" and "Indecent Proposal" and was nominated for an Oscar for "The Substance".
bio|11-11|1966|Μπενεντίκτα Μπόκκολι|Benedetta Boccoli|Benedetta Boccoli is an Italian actress and presenter, known for films and television series in Italy.

bio|11-11|1974|Λεονάρντο Ντι Κάπριο|Leonardo DiCaprio|Leonardo DiCaprio is an American actor. He became known for "Titanic" and won an Oscar for "The Revenant". He is also involved in the protection of the environment.

bio|11-11|1976|Αλεξάντερ Κάλντερ|Alexander Calder|Alexander Calder was an American sculptor. He invented the "mobiles", kinetic sculptures that hang and move with the currents of air. He died in 1976.

bio|11-11|2004|Γιάσερ Αραφάτ|Yasser Arafat|Yasser Arafat died in 2004 in a hospital in Paris. He was the leader of the Palestine Liberation Organization and the first president of the Palestinian Authority.

bio|11-11|683|Γιαζίντ Α΄|Yazid I|Yazid I was caliph of the Umayyad dynasty, from 680 to 683. His reign is known for the battle of Karbala, where Hussein was killed, and for the uprisings that followed.
bio|11-12|1035|Κανούτος|Cnut the Great|Cnut the Great was king of England from 1016, and also of Denmark and Norway. He ruled a large northern empire. He died in 1035.
bio|11-12|1840|Ογκίστ Ροντέν|Auguste Rodin|Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor. He created the works "The Thinker", "The Kiss" and "The Gates of Hell". He died in 1917.

bio|11-12|1866|Σουν Γιατ-Σεν|Sun Yat-sen|Sun Yat-sen was a Chinese revolutionary and politician. He led the Revolution of 1911, which overthrew the Qing dynasty, and was the first provisional president of the Republic of China. He died in 1925.

bio|11-12|1916|Πέρσιβαλ Λόουελ|Percival Lowell|Percival Lowell was an American astronomer. He founded the Lowell Observatory and studied Mars, wrongly arguing that there were "canals" there. He died in 1916.

bio|11-12|1929|Γκρέις Κέλι|Grace Kelly|Grace Kelly was an American actress. She won an Oscar for "The Country Girl" and in 1956 she married Prince Rainier III of Monaco. She was killed in a car accident in 1982.

bio|11-12|1948|Χασάν Ρουχανί|Hassan Rouhani|Hassan Rouhani is an Iranian politician and cleric. He was president of Iran from 2013 to 2021 and negotiated the agreement on the nuclear programme in 2015.
bio|11-12|1981|Γουίλιαμ Χόλντεν|William Holden|William Holden was an American actor. He won an Oscar for "Stalag 17" and appeared in "Sunset Boulevard". He died in 1981.
bio|11-12|1982|Αν Χάθαγουεϊ|Anne Hathaway|Anne Hathaway is an American actress. She won an Oscar for "Les Misérables" and appeared in "The Devil Wears Prada".

bio|11-13|354|Αυγουστίνος της Ιππώνος|Augustine of Hippo|Augustine of Hippo was born in 354 in Thagaste, in Africa. He became a bishop and an important theologian of the West. He wrote the "Confessions" and "The City of God". He died in 430.
bio|11-13|1312|Εδουάρδος Γ΄|Edward III|Edward III was king of England from 1327 to 1377. He began the Hundred Years' War with France and the English won the battle of Crécy. He died in 1377.

bio|11-13|1460|Ερρίκος ο Θαλασσοπόρος|Henry the Navigator|Henry the Navigator was a Portuguese prince. He supported Portuguese expeditions along the African coast and so paved the way for the discoveries. He died in 1460.

bio|06-13|1831|Τζέιμς Κλερκ Μάξγουελ|James Clerk Maxwell|James Clerk Maxwell was born in 1831 in Edinburgh. He was a physicist and mathematician who united electricity, magnetism and light in his equations. He died in 1879.

bio|11-13|1850|Ρόμπερτ Λούις Στίβενσον|Robert Louis Stevenson|Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish writer. He wrote "Treasure Island" and "The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde". He died in 1894, in Samoa.
bio|11-13|1868|Τζοακίνο Ροσσίνι|Gioachino Rossini|Gioachino Rossini was an Italian composer. He wrote the operas "The Barber of Seville" and "William Tell". He died in 1868.
bio|11-13|1903|Καμίλ Πισαρό|Camille Pissarro|Camille Pissarro was a French painter and one of the pioneers of Impressionism. He painted landscapes and scenes of Paris. He died in 1903.

bio|11-13|1955|Γούπι Γκόλντμπεργκ|Whoopi Goldberg|Whoopi Goldberg is an American actress and comedian. She won an Oscar for "Ghost" and is one of the few people to have won an Oscar, an Emmy, a Grammy and a Tony.
bio|11-13|1974|Βιττόριο ντε Σίκα|Vittorio De Sica|Vittorio De Sica was an Italian director and actor of Neorealism. He directed "Bicycle Thieves". He died in 1974.

bio|11-14|1263|Αλέξανδρος Νιέφσκι|Alexander Nevsky|Alexander Nevsky was prince of Novgorod and grand prince of Vladimir. He defeated the Swedes on the Neva in 1240 and the Teutonic Knights on the frozen Lake Peipus. The Russian Church honours him as a saint.

bio|11-14|1716|Γκότφριντ Βίλχελμ Λάιμπνιτς|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was a German philosopher and mathematician. He developed infinitesimal calculus independently of Newton. He died in 1716 in Hanover.

bio|11-14|1831|Γκέοργκ Βίλχελμ Φρήντριχ Χέγκελ|Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel|Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a German philosopher of idealism. He wrote the "Phenomenology of Spirit". He died in 1831, possibly of cholera.

bio|11-14|1840|Κλοντ Μονέ|Claude Monet|Claude Monet was a French painter and a leading figure of Impressionism. His work "Impression, Sunrise" gave the movement its name. He painted the "Water Lilies". He died in 1926.

bio|11-14|1889|Τζαβαχαρλάλ Νεχρού|Jawaharlal Nehru|Jawaharlal Nehru was the first prime minister of India, from 1947 to 1964. He was a close collaborator of Gandhi in the struggle for independence. He died in 1964.
bio|11-14|1907|Άστριντ Λίντγκρεν|Astrid Lindgren|Astrid Lindgren was a Swedish author of children's books. She created "Pippi Longstocking", "Emil" and "The Brothers Lionheart". She died in 2002.

bio|11-14|1948|Κάρολος|King Charles III|Charles III was born in 1948. He was Prince of Wales for more than 60 years and became king of the United Kingdom in 2022, after the death of his mother Elizabeth II.
bio|11-14|1972|Τζος Ντουχάμελ|Josh Duhamel|Josh Duhamel is an American actor. He became known with the series "Las Vegas" and with films such as "Transformers".

bio|11-15|1630|Γιοχάνες Κέπλερ|Johannes Kepler|Johannes Kepler was a German astronomer and mathematician. He formulated the three laws of planetary motion, based on the observations of Tycho Brahe. He died in 1630.

bio|11-15|1670|Ιωάννης Αμός Κομένιος|Jan Amos Comenius|Jan Amos Comenius was a Czech educator and theologian. He is regarded as the "father of modern education" and wrote "Orbis pictus", an illustrated school book. He died in 1670.

bio|11-15|1738|Ουίλιαμ Χέρσελ|William Herschel|William Herschel was born in Germany and lived in England. He was an astronomer and a composer. In 1781 he discovered the planet Uranus. He died in 1822.
bio|11-15|1862|Γκέρχαρτ Χάουπτμαν|Gerhart Hauptmann|Gerhart Hauptmann was a German playwright. He wrote "The Weavers" and in 1912 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1946.
bio|11-15|1887|Τζόρτζια Ο'Κιφ|Georgia O'Keeffe|Georgia O'Keeffe was an American painter. She became known for paintings of large flowers and for the desert landscapes of New Mexico. She died in 1986.

bio|11-15|1891|Έρβιν Ρόμελ|Erwin Rommel|Erwin Rommel was a German field marshal, known as the "Desert Fox". He commanded the Afrika Korps and was later linked to the conspiracy against Hitler. He died in 1944.
bio|11-15|1916|Χένρικ Σιενκιέβιτς|Henryk Sienkiewicz|Henryk Sienkiewicz was a Polish writer. He wrote "Quo Vadis" and in 1905 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1916.

bio|11-15|1917|Εμίλ Ντιρκέμ|Émile Durkheim|Émile Durkheim was a French sociologist and one of the founders of sociology. He wrote "Suicide" and "The Elementary Forms of Religious Life". He died in 1917.
bio|11-15|1993|Πάουλο Ντιμπάλα|Paulo Dybala|Paulo Dybala is an Argentine footballer, a striker. He played for Juventus and Roma and won the World Cup in 2022.
bio|11-16|1272|Ερρίκος Γ΄|Henry III|Henry III was king of England from 1216 to 1272, one of the longest reigns. He came to the throne as a child and rebuilt Westminster Abbey. He died in 1272.

bio|11-16|1632|Γουσταύος Β΄ Αδόλφος|Gustavus Adolphus|Gustavus II Adolphus was king of Sweden from 1611. He led the Protestant army in the Thirty Years' War and was killed at the battle of Lützen in 1632.

bio|11-16|1717|Ζαν λε Ροντ ντ' Αλαμπέρ|Jean le Rond d'Alembert|Jean le Rond d'Alembert was a French mathematician and philosopher of the Enlightenment. He co-edited the "Encyclopédie" with Diderot. He died in 1783.

bio|11-16|1922|Ζοζέ Σαραμάγκου|José Saramago|José Saramago was a Portuguese writer. He wrote the novels "Blindness" and "The Gospel According to Jesus Christ", and in 1998 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2010.

bio|11-16|1930|Τσινούα Ατσέμπε|Chinua Achebe|Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian writer. His novel "Things Fall Apart", about colonialism in Africa, became one of the best-known African books. He died in 2013.

bio|11-16|1960|Κλαρκ Γκέιμπλ|Clark Gable|Clark Gable was an American actor, known as "the King of Hollywood". He played Rhett Butler in "Gone with the Wind" and won an Oscar for "It Happened One Night". He died in 1960.
bio|11-16|1974|Πολ Σκόουλς|Paul Scholes|Paul Scholes is a former English footballer, a midfielder. He played his entire career for Manchester United and won 11 Premier League titles.

bio|11-16|1977|Μάγκι Τζίλενχαλ|Maggie Gyllenhaal|Maggie Gyllenhaal is an American actress. She appeared in "Secretary", "The Lost Daughter" and "The Dark Knight", and she is the sister of the actor Jake Gyllenhaal.
